later_events.mechanism: revocation_of_the_revoking_order_with_saving: EO 9695 (February 8, 1946; 11 FR 1559) revokes EO 9243 and provides that the revocation shall not affect reemployment rights acquired under EO 8973 and EO 9067. It does not revive EO 9067, whose revocation by EO 9243 had taken effect on September 27, 1942.

termination_of_reemployment_rights: EO 9952 (April 22, 1948), held Federal Register text, section 1 provides that existing reemployment rights acquired under authority of EO 9067, among other instruments, expire at the end of six months from its date unless application is made. It acts on rights already acquired and is not an end of this order.

amendment_of_termination_of_reemployment_rights: EO 9994 (September 1, 1948), held APP transcription, amends section 1 of EO 9952 so that those reemployment rights expire on October 22, 1948, with provisos for employees in agencies being liquidated and for persons separated from the armed forces or merchant marine. It acts on rights already acquired and is not an end of this order.

research_rationale:
EO 9067 (February 20, 1942, Franklin D. Roosevelt; 7 FR 1407, issue of Wednesday, February 25, 1942, PDF pages 1-3) "Providing for the Transfer of Personnel to War Agencies" is read in full in the held Federal Register text. The machine inventory for this order covers the neighbouring order on military areas, so the inventory is replaced by the order's six numbered sections: priority classifications by the Director of the Bureau of the Budget (1), Civil Service Commission transfers with the employee's consent (2), the ten-day transfer rule and the consent rule for equal or lower classifications (3), reemployment benefits under EO 8973 for transferred employees (4), Commission rules and agency information duties (5), and supersession of conflicting provisions of EO 8973 and other orders (6). The order states no term. EO 9243 (September 12, 1942), held only as an American Presidency Project transcription (Common Crawl capture 2026-01-13; a provisional working text), revokes EO 9067 by number in its section 3, effective on the fifteenth day after its date, September 27, 1942, and saves reemployment rights already acquired. That is the first end for every section.

savings.reason: Reemployment rights acquired by employees transferred under EO 9067 before September 27, 1942 survive the revocation: EO 9243 section 3 provides that nothing in it "shall be construed to affect reemployment rights theretofore acquired by any employee under Executive Orders Nos. 8973 and 9067". These are rights already acquired, separate from the order's commands. Later orders acted on those rights and not on EO 9067: EO 9695 (February 8, 1946) repeated the saving, EO 9952 (April 22, 1948) made existing rights expire six months after its date unless application was made, and EO 9994 (September 1, 1948) changed that expiry to October 22, 1948 with two provisos; all three are listed as later events on section 4.
